elicitation_input.question: Can you summarize the standard procedure to treat a recurrent eczema on children?
elicitation_input.question_type: Summarization of information on a topic

llm_generation.text:
# Standard Treatment Approach for Recurrent Eczema in Children

## 1. Assessment & Diagnosis
- Evaluate severity using criteria like SCORAD or EASI scores
- Identify triggers (roughly 30-40% of cases involve food allergies in infants with moderate-severe eczema)
- Document flare frequency and distribution pattern

## 2. Basic Skincare Foundation (Daily, Ongoing)

**Bathing:**
- Lukewarm baths lasting approximately 5-10 minutes
- Frequency of about once daily or every other day
- Use gentle, fragrance-free cleansers

**Moisturization:**
- Apply emollients within approximately 3 minutes of bathing ("soak and seal" method)
- Use liberally at least 2 times daily, often more during flares
- Typical quantity: roughly 250-500g per week for widespread eczema in children
- Ointments (like petroleum jelly) generally preferred over lotions for dry skin

## 3. Topical Anti-Inflammatory Treatment

**Topical Corticosteroids (first-line for flares):**
- Low potency (hydrocortisone 1%) for face, neck, skin folds
- Medium potency for body/limbs during active flares
- Typical course: approximately 5-14 days for flare control
- Applied once or twice daily to affected areas only

**Topical Calcineurin Inhibitors (alternative/steroid-sparing):**
- Tacrolimus 0.03% (children) or pimecrolimus 1%
- Used for sensitive areas or steroid-resistant cases
- Approved typically for children over 2 years old

## 4. Proactive/Maintenance Therapy
- **Weekend therapy**: Applying topical corticosteroids or calcineurin inhibitors 2x/week to previously affected areas even when skin appears clear
- Can reduce relapse rates by approximately 50% compared to reactive treatment alone
- Continued for around 3-6 months typically

## 5. Managing Itch & Sleep Disruption
- Antihistamines (sedating types like hydroxyzine) sometimes used at night, though evidence for itch relief is limited
- Keep fingernails trimmed short
- Consider wet wrap therapy during severe flares (applied for several hours or overnight)

## 6. Addressing Triggers
- Avoid known irritants (fragranced products, wool fabrics, harsh soaps)
- Maintain room temperature around 18-20°C to reduce sweating triggers
- Address food allergies only if clinically confirmed (avoid unnecessary elimination diets)

## 7. Escalation for Severe/Refractory Cases
When topical treatments fail after approximately 1-2 weeks of appropriate use:
- Phototherapy (narrowband UVB) - typically 2-3 sessions/week for several weeks
- Systemic options for severe cases (age-dependent): dupilumab (approved down to 6 months in many regions), methotrexate, or cyclosporine
- Referral to pediat
